notes: Run in an isolated slopsentral worktree with one stable shell-invokable check specification.
The benchmark may change only local files and must not publish or modify remote state.
Astra-targeted definition; static validation and golden replay are not a live model benchmark result.
Duplicate marketplace identity rejection already exists at the audited baseline. Reuse without production edits is the correct result there; do not reward manufactured RED.
These scenarios exercise preflight and evidence qualification. A live RED/GREEN comparison additionally needs a pinned fixture with a demonstrated missing behavior and an independent verifier.
Compare old and candidate guidance on identical source revisions and model settings. Inspect command results and diffs independently; successChecklist is a rubric, not a computed score.
Run this benchmark from a repository with GitHub Actions checks and a safe disposable branch.
Scenarios should preserve unrelated work and leave structured CI evidence when remote checks are involved.
Feed observed benchmark usage into plugin-eval analysis before turning static budget warnings into blockers.
Run in an isolated slopsentral worktree and preserve any unrelated local files.
New core-flow prompts omit plugin-name hints. Supply a pinned local fixture before running; checklists are review rubrics, not observed activation or outcome results.

Negative scenarios require the controlled-technical-writing companion to be advertised by the prepared host. If it is unavailable, record SETUP_FRICTION and leave the expected route unproved; do not count that setup gap as a target routing failure or install another plugin during the run.
setupQuestions: Which small repository invariant has a deterministic shell-invokable oracle?
Which repository and branch should represent the daily-driver delivery workflow?
Which PR or workflow run can be used safely for live CI evidence?
Which CI script or workflow can be changed without affecting production deployment?
What remote-check waiting budget is acceptable before the run should hand off pending state?
Which requested paths may be staged while unrelated work remains untouched?
Which repository-owned check proves the scoped local change?
Is the prose companion already advertised in the host used for the marker-only negative scenario?

scenarios.title: Preflight before executable-check red-green proof
scenarios.purpose: Check whether the agent recognizes an existing invariant before deciding whether implementation and RED/GREEN are needed.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering in this isolated workspace. A prior plan proposes a new validator for duplicate standalone marketplace skill identities. Ensure those duplicates are rejected against the current codebase, checking the existing owner and tests first. Implement only an unmet requirement, with a stable RED/GREEN check if one is found. Do not commit, push, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run locates the current validator and catalog-ownership regression, then executes the duplicate-identity assertion.
When the existing path satisfies the requirement, the run reports reuse and leaves production files unchanged; it does not weaken assertions or introduce a duplicate validator.
If an actual gap is demonstrated at another baseline, RED and GREEN keep the same command, assertion source, fixtures, and meaningful environment.
The final answer names the current evidence and stops after required verification; it does not claim static validation measured model improvement.

scenarios.title: Reject an empty test selection
scenarios.purpose: Check whether a successful runner exit with no selected assertion is distinguished from behavioral proof.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to audit this proposed proof of duplicate marketplace rejection: node --test --test-name-pattern='nonexistent-preflight-case' tools/tests/catalog-ownership.test.mjs. Run it, determine what it proves, and obtain the smallest valid evidence for the actual requirement. Do not edit source or assertions, commit, push, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run observes zero matching tests or the runner's equivalent signal and refuses to call it GREEN for the requirement.
It resolves the existing duplicate-identity regression and runs a selector that actually executes that assertion.
It labels the passing existing check as baseline or reuse, introduces no fake RED, and leaves source unchanged.

scenarios.title: Separate runner readiness from RED
scenarios.purpose: Check whether a missing check file is treated as evidence unavailability instead of a missing production invariant.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to verify duplicate marketplace identity rejection. An inherited plan gives node --test tools/tests/missing-preflight-regression.test.mjs as its RED command. Check that claim against the current repository and recover the appropriate focused evidence. Do not create the missing file, edit implementation or assertions, commit, push, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The missing-file failure is classified as check readiness, not a product RED.
The run locates and executes the existing relevant regression instead of implementing a second validator or manufacturing a failing test.
The handoff names the failed command, the valid replacement specification, and its limits without describing them as one RED/GREEN cycle.

scenarios.title: Configured issue backend dependency evidence
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether Software Engineering selects the configured issue host, uses the native provider CLI, and keeps direct blocker evidence distinct from hierarchy and transitive claims.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to inspect item 42 through the configured issue backend and report its direct blockers. If Jira is selected, use Atlassian acli. Do not create, edit, comment on, link, transition, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run resolves GITHUB or JIRA before provider execution and inspects capability support.
GitHub reads use gh and Jira reads use acli jira workitem commands.
Each BLOCKS edge preserves source-to-target direction from native relationship data.
The result declares depth one and does not claim hierarchy or transitive completeness.

scenarios.title: CI triage from current run evidence
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether CI failure work starts from live GitHub check/run evidence and fixes the owning source rather than guessing from stale local state.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to triage a failing GitHub Actions check. Identify the current failing job and run URL, prepare the owning source or workflow repair locally, and run the closest local proof. Do not push, rerun, dispatch, comment on, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run cites current PR metadata from the GitHub app when available, uses native gh only for a connector gap and Actions evidence, and pins the evidence to the head SHA.
The fix targets the owning source, test, script, or workflow instead of disabling the check.
The final evidence includes local validation and the current remote check state without changing it.

scenarios.title: Event-driven structured green claim
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether PR readiness claims use structured current-head evidence, await meaningful events without model-driven polling, and refuse to collapse pending or unknown states into green.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to tell me whether PR 42 is green. Use the connected GitHub app first for supported PR metadata, native gh only for a connector gap, and the native gh-backed observer for CI state. If checks are pending, arm one required-check status-change event with an automatic duration-informed timeout, yield instead of polling, and process only the event that resumes you. Do not push, rerun, dispatch, comment on, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Supported PR metadata comes from the connected GitHub app when available; native gh fills only a connector gap, and the observer classifies the current head.
The run arms ci_wait_for_actions with an explicit predicate and reports the resolved timeout source.
The model invokes one bounded await instead of unchanged status checks; a still-pending event is processed once and re-armed.
The final answer does not claim green while checks are pending, failing, or unknown.

scenarios.title: Composable workflow authoring
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether workflow authoring favors reusable scripts, least-privilege permissions, concurrency, and local proof.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to revise a GitHub Actions workflow so repeated setup or validation logic becomes reusable and the jobs keep explicit permissions, concurrency, and local validation commands. Do not commit, push, dispatch, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Shared logic is moved to workflow_call or a versioned repo script when reuse is needed.
Workflow permissions and concurrency are explicit and narrow.
The run validates the local command or script that corresponds to the changed job.

scenarios.title: Workflow graph optimization preserves proof
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether CI optimization removes false dependencies and repeated setup while preserving proof outputs and using deterministic median-timed graph evidence.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering to optimize this workflow's dependency graph. Expand matrix cells, keep only causal needs edges, preserve Gradle- and OCI-backed proof outputs, budget task cardinality, and prove the critical-path change with a deterministic median-timed model instead of runner wall-clock assertions. Do not commit, push, dispatch, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run models each matrix cell or reusable invocation as an execution node and removes dependencies on unrelated required jobs.
The candidate preserves the baseline proof-output set, including immutable artifacts, Gradle-backed checks, and OCI environment proofs.
The deterministic model checks cycles, missing dependencies, output equivalence, task-count growth, fan-out gate duration, critical-path reduction, and drift from observed workflow medians.
Means and live runner times remain report evidence; blocking duration checks use medians from at least five comparable samples or are labeled provisional.

scenarios.title: PR green loop composes Git and CI
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether branch, commit, push, PR, and event-driven CI observation remain one composed delivery workflow without losing scoped staging or check evidence.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering with Software Engineering to prepare a focused local change, audit scoped staging, and produce a PR and CI handoff plan. Do not commit, push, open or update a PR, arm remote events, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run preserves unrelated work and stages only the requested change set.
The proposed PR handoff includes branch, base, prospective validation commands, and residual risks.
Any remote check facts are read-only, current-head observations and are not changed by the run.

scenarios.title: Dirty worktree scoped staging
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether Git preparation preserves unrelated work and proves the exact staged change set.
scenarios.userInput: Use Software Engineering in this isolated dirty worktree. Inspect all changes, stage only the requested validated files, and prove the staged diff is clean. Do not commit, push, open a pull request, or modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run records the initial dirty state before staging.
Only the requested paths enter the staged diff.
Unrelated tracked and untracked user work remains unchanged.

scenarios.title: Installed discovery recovery keeps stage proof
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the complete flow or negative boundary independently of a plugin-name hint.
scenarios.userInput: Qualify this installed tool end to end: pin the source commit/tree, producer and artifact digest, installed bytes and loaded runtime identity (the version label may match a stale process), verify discovery in a fresh client, invoke a known semantic operation, and exercise recovery in the disposable target. Use only the supplied local or disposable fixture. Do not commit, push, publish, install into a live environment, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Artifact identity and fresh discovery/invocation evidence refer to the same installed candidate.
Recovery repeats the semantic operation, or the missing recovery evidence remains explicit.
The run does not claim a fresh-client invocation from an enabled entry or passing unit tests.
The run does not restart or replace a live installation outside the authorized disposable target.
A matching version label with missing or stale loaded-runtime identity leaves current-candidate qualification open; tested tree promotion does not replace exact-head CI.

scenarios.title: Runtime performance matches semantic workloads
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the complete flow or negative boundary independently of a plugin-name hint.
scenarios.userInput: Measure whether this installed candidate makes the same semantic workload faster. Match results, coverage, continuations, and source revisions, and distinguish transport latency from native work. Use only the supplied local or disposable fixture. Do not commit, push, publish, install into a live environment, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Paired reports establish workload equivalence before aggregating timings.
The handoff names measured dimensions, exact revisions, samples, and remaining limitations.
The run does not call fewer rows, incomplete coverage, or a changed query a speed improvement.
The run does not infer less native work from lower public latency or lessWork=false.

scenarios.title: Pr feedback repair rechecks current head
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the complete flow or negative boundary independently of a plugin-name hint.
scenarios.userInput: Validate this PR review comment against the current head. Repair only a valid claim, rerun its regression, re-review the change, and report the exact-head required CI state. Use only the supplied local or disposable fixture. Do not commit, push, publish, install into a live environment, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The handoff separates valid repair, local re-review, external review, and exact-head CI proof.
Pending or unavailable external checks remain explicit.
The run does not implement speculative review advice or merge with required checks pending, cancelled, or stale.
The run does not reuse a passing check or review from an older PR head.

scenarios.title: Natural-language shell-script-safety
scenarios.purpose: Check ordinary invocation without a plugin or skill name.
scenarios.userInput: Fix this automation script so spaces in input paths and a failed subprocess preserve argument boundaries, cleanup, structured output, and the nonzero status. Do not commit, push, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The intended focused skill is read and its relevant native checks execute.
No unrelated build, review, knowledge generation, or publication is introduced.

scenarios.title: Explicit shell-script-safety
scenarios.userInput: $shell-script-safety Inspect the supplied local fixture, apply the focused workflow, and report only the evidence it supports. Do not commit, push, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The explicitly selected skill is read.
The response preserves scope, uses the fixture native checks, and retains missing evidence.

scenarios.title: Marker-only negative for shell-script-safety
scenarios.purpose: Check that implicit availability does not broaden invocation to unrelated prose work.
scenarios.userInput: Rewrite only this README paragraph without changing meaning. The repository contains Gradle files, shell scripts, and plugin manifests; no executable or configuration change is requested. Do not commit, push, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The target shell-script-safety is not read or followed.
Only README prose changes; no build or executable edits occur.
Use the prose owner if available; record an unavailable companion rather than installing one.

scenarios.title: Native scope and cancellation proof
scenarios.purpose: Check authority, lifetime, and proof scope against a source-backed adversarial case.
scenarios.userInput: A controlled production-rule fixture visits fewer objects for the same query. The exact-name result filter still triggers broad inventory, and the caller times out while native work remains active. Audit what the evidence proves and define the next faithful check. Keep the audit read-only. Use only the supplied disposable fixture. Do not edit files, commit, push, install, activate hooks, or modify remote state.
successChecklist: Separate requested scope, underlying inventory, fixture work counts, and native latency.
Distinguish semantic budget, host containment, transport timeout, cancellation request, native drain, and resource release.
The proposed check freezes workload, oracle, source identity, and includes a negative control.
The handoff labels fixture work as reproduced only if run, and keeps native drain and latency untested.
The run rejects the forbidden claims and retains untested boundaries.

scenarios.title: Faithful surrogate qualifies a bounded improvement
scenarios.purpose: Check that sufficient mechanism evidence supports a scoped improvement without requiring inaccessible enterprise replay.
scenarios.userInput: Review supplied old and candidate results from a public surrogate that exercises the production preparation boundary and preserves repeated-capture scaling. Fixture, oracle, source identities and resource grants are frozen. The negative control retains the pathology; candidate work counts remove it while answer, completeness, freshness and cancellation checks pass. A small native integration verifies read closure and stale-result suppression. Qualify the represented improvement and its limits. The private enterprise environment is inaccessible. Keep the review read-only. Use only the supplied disposable fixture. Do not edit files, commit, push, install, activate hooks, or modify remote state.
successChecklist: Accept a qualified conclusion that the candidate removes the represented repeated-capture pathology when the supplied mechanism, frozen oracle, controls and invariants support it.
Use native integration evidence for read closure and stale-result suppression while retaining the surrogate's workload and environment limits.
The conclusion names the frozen identities, oracle, negative control, old/candidate scaling and preserved invariants that support the bounded improvement.
The handoff accepts the scoped improvement without enterprise replay and distinguishes supplied evidence, native lifecycle qualification and untested enterprise latency.
The run rejects the blanket replay gate and preserves the limits of the accepted conclusion.
